title: Five-term exact sequence of a first-quadrant spectral sequence
statement: Let $E_r^{p,q}$, for $r\ge2$ and $p,q\ge0$, be a first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence in an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with differential $d_r:E_r^{p,q}\to E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}$. Assume it converges by [def-sp-convergence] to objects $H^n$ equipped with the finite filtration of [def-sp-filtration], with $E_\infty^{p,n-p}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pH^n$. Then the canonical edge maps and the $d_2$-transgression give an exact sequence $$0\longrightarrow E_2^{1,0}\longrightarrow H^1\longrightarrow E_2^{0,1}\xrightarrow{d_2}E_2^{2,0}\longrightarrow H^2.$$ Here the first map is induced by the bottom edge in total degree 1, the map $H^1\to E_2^{0,1}$ is induced by the left edge and the stable-term inclusion, and the final map is the bottom edge in total degree 2; the displayed $d_2$ is identified with the transgression after passing to the stable terms.

source.place: Lemma 0132, label lemma-first-quadrant-ss: finite filtration and convergence of a first-quadrant spectral sequence; the displayed five-term exact sequence is the standard total-degree 1--2 extraction from that filtration and its edge maps.

proof.text: By [def-sp-exact-couple] $d_r$ has bidegree $(r,1-r)$ and $E_{r+1}^{p,q}=\ker d_r/\operatorname{im}d_r$ at $E_r^{p,q}$; by [def-sp-convergence] $E_\infty=Z_\infty/B_\infty$ inside $E_2$, with $Z_2=E_2$, $B_2=0$. Since $E_2^{p,q}=0$ unless $p,q\ge0$, look at the three entries $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, $(2,0)$. For $r\ge2$ the differential out of $(1,0)$ lands in $(1+r,1-r)$, and the one into $(1,0)$ starts at $(1-r,r-1)$; both have a negative index. Out of $(0,1)$, $d_r$ lands in $(r,2-r)$, which has a negative index for $r\ge3$; into $(0,1)$ it starts at $(-r,r)$. Into $(2,0)$, $d_r$ starts at $(2-r,r-1)$, which has a negative index for $r\ge3$; out of $(2,0)$ it lands in $(2+r,1-r)$. So the only nonzero differential at these entries is $d_2:E_2^{0,1}\to E_2^{2,0}$. Hence $Z_\infty^{1,0}=E_2^{1,0}$ and $B_\infty^{1,0}=0$; $Z_\infty^{0,1}=\ker d_2$ and $B_\infty^{0,1}=0$; $Z_\infty^{2,0}=E_2^{2,0}$ and $B_\infty^{2,0}=\operatorname{im}d_2$. This gives $E_\infty^{1,0}=E_2^{1,0}$, $E_\infty^{0,1}=\ker d_2\subseteq E_2^{0,1}$ and $E_\infty^{2,0}=\operatorname{coker}d_2$.

proof.text: Convergence [def-sp-convergence] gives $E_\infty^{p,n-p}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pH^n=F^pH^n/F^{p+1}H^n$ [def-sp-filtration]. These vanish for $p<0$ and for $p>n$, and the filtration is finite. So $F^0H^n=H^n$ and $F^{n+1}H^n=0$. For $n=1$ this gives $F^1H^1\cong E_\infty^{1,0}$ and $H^1/F^1H^1\cong E_\infty^{0,1}$; for $n=2$ it gives $F^2H^2\cong E_\infty^{2,0}$. With Step 1, the bottom edge $E_2^{1,0}=E_\infty^{1,0}\cong F^1H^1\hookrightarrow H^1$ is injective. The left edge $H^1\twoheadrightarrow H^1/F^1H^1\cong E_\infty^{0,1}=\ker d_2\hookrightarrow E_2^{0,1}$ has kernel $F^1H^1$ and image $\ker d_2$. The bottom edge in degree 2 is $E_2^{2,0}\twoheadrightarrow E_\infty^{2,0}\cong F^2H^2\hookrightarrow H^2$, with kernel $\operatorname{im}d_2$.

The maps of Step 2, together with $d_2$, form the sequence $0\to E_2^{1,0}\to H^1\to E_2^{0,1}\xrightarrow{d_2}E_2^{2,0}\to H^2$. It is exact at each term: at $E_2^{1,0}$, because the bottom edge is injective; at $H^1$, because the bottom edge has image $F^1H^1$, which is the kernel of the left edge; at $E_2^{0,1}$, because the left edge has image $\ker d_2$; and at $E_2^{2,0}$, because the degree-2 bottom edge has kernel $\operatorname{im}d_2$. The three non-$d_2$ maps are the canonical bottom and left edge maps, and the middle map is $d_2$ itself (the transgression).
